question: On 15 April 2026, the Commission unveiled a digital app for age verification online1. The Commission President described the functioning of the EU age verification app as ‘completely anonymous’. However, there are significant doubts as to whether the complete anonymity claimed by the Commission can actually be guaranteed in practice. 1.

How will the Commission ensure that, when implementing the measure at national level, issuing authorities do not carry out any form of logging that would allow individual users to be identified, and what control and verification mechanisms will be put in place to effectively monitor compliance in the Member States with the anonymity guarantee claimed by the Commission?

What binding technical and legal requirements exist to prevent additional metadata such as IP addresses, device identifiers or timestamps from being collected, stored or analysed in the applications or the associated backend systems?
How will the Commission ensure that the age verification function is not linked to other state or private systems, thereby enabling subsequent identification or profiling?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (23.6.2026) To ensure that data protection and security requirements are fulfilled, age verification solutions will be assessed and approved by the Commission in accordance with Commission Recommendation (EU) 2026/10351.

The rules and requirements for the assessment will be established in the age verification attestation of attributes scheme based on Article 8 of Implementing Regulation (EU) 1569/20252, the Age Verification Blueprint3, the Electronic Identification, Authentication and Trust Services Regulation (eIDAS)4, the Network and Information Security Directive5, the Cyber Resilience Act6 and the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)7.

Providers of EU age verification solutions are trust service providers under eIDAS8 and they are required to set up internal risk management processes and notify the Commission of any security breaches. Their operations are subject to supervision by national authorities. GDPR ensures that data protection rights of citizens are protected, and this applies to age verification providers.

Age verification solutions must not communicate any information identifying the user. Any privacy invasive measures are prohibited, and compliance will be assessed by the Commission and national supervisory authorities. It is technically not possible to keep IP addresses, device identifiers or timestamps fully private.
However, EU age verification solutions ensure that this kind of information cannot be linked to the identity of the person who uses them.
